explanations.explanation: That's it, friend. Daniel 10:1 says the message was true and it concerned a great conflict. The understanding of it was given to him in a vision. Verse one wastes no time telling us this isn't a light read.

A harvest sounds cozy, I'll give you that. But Daniel 10:1 says the message was true and it concerned a great conflict. That's a different kind of message altogether. The understanding of it came to Daniel in a vision.

No suitcase needed on this one, friend. Daniel 10:1 says the message was true and it concerned a great conflict. Nothing about packing or traveling in that verse. The understanding of it was given to him in a vision.

Yes, friend. Daniel says, "I ate no rich food, no meat or wine entered my mouth, and I did not anoint myself with oil until the three weeks were completed" (Daniel 10:3). That's a long stretch without a single treat. I can't walk past my own cooling rack without a taste test, so this one humbles me.

Daniel 10:3 says the opposite: "I ate no rich food…" He also had no meat or wine, and he went without anointing himself with oil until the three weeks were completed. So the statement on the card holds. Me, I'd last about an hour away from my own dough.
The Tigris, friend. Daniel 10:4 puts him on the bank of the great river, the Tigris, on the twenty-fourth day of the first month. That's where he is when he lifts up his eyes in the very next verse.

The Jordan is a fine river, but it's not the one in this verse. Daniel 10:4 says he's on the bank of the great river, the Tigris. That's where he's standing on the twenty-fourth day of the first month.
Daniel 10:4 names the great river as the Tigris, not the Nile. Same riverbank scene, different name than the one you picked, friend. He's standing there on the twenty-fourth day of the first month.

Ordinary? Not by a long shot, friend. Daniel 10:6 says "his face like the brilliance of lightning, his eyes like flaming torches…" His arms and legs gleam like polished bronze, too. If a man like that showed up at my bakery door, I'd hand him whatever he asked for.

Not ordinary at all. Daniel 10:6 says "his face like the brilliance of lightning, his eyes like flaming torches…" Even my oven door doesn't glow like that. Whoever this is, he's not blending into the crowd.

That's what they do. Daniel 10:7 says they didn't see the vision, but "a great terror fell upon them, and they ran and hid themselves." Their feet made the decision before their heads got a vote. That leaves Daniel alone with it (Daniel 10:8).

That's not what the men do, friend. Daniel 10:7 says "they ran and hid themselves." The one who ends up face to the ground is Daniel, when he falls into a deep sleep (Daniel 10:9). The men are not around for that part, since Daniel says he was left alone (Daniel 10:8).

explanations.answer: They call out to the man
explanations.explanation: Nobody's calling out to anybody here. Daniel 10:7 says "they ran and hid themselves." That's about as far from a friendly hello as you can get. Daniel says he was left alone, gazing at the vision (Daniel 10:8).

Nothing left in the tank. Daniel says, "No strength remained in me; my face grew deathly pale, and I was powerless" (Daniel 10:8). That's me after a double batch in a holiday week, only a lot more serious.
Not quite, friend. Daniel 10:8 says, "No strength remained in me," and he's left powerless. That's a big change from where he started. Strength does come back to him later (Daniel 10:18).

It goes the other direction. Daniel 10:8 says, "No strength remained in me; my face grew deathly pale, and I was powerless." He's about as far from stronger as a person can get. Someone strengthens him later on (Daniel 10:18).

Staying upright would be impressive, but Daniel 10:9 says, "as I listened, I fell into a deep sleep, with my face to the ground." His strength was already gone (Daniel 10:8), so I think that tracks. My own knees would have filed a complaint much sooner.
He doesn't stay standing, friend. Daniel 10:9 says, "as I listened, I fell into a deep sleep, with my face to the ground." So down he goes. I'd have gone down sooner, and with a lot more noise.

explanations.answer: He has now been sent to Daniel
explanations.explanation: That's the reason he gives. He says, "Stand up, for I have now been sent to you" (Daniel 10:11). Right before that, he tells Daniel to consider carefully the words he's about to say. A visitor with a message, and Daniel is who it's for.

The speaker never mentions Daniel's men here, friend. They ran and hid back in Daniel 10:7, and nothing in verse 11 talks about them returning. The reason he gives is "for I have now been sent to you."

explanations.answer: The three weeks are not over
explanations.explanation: Nothing about the three weeks comes up in this moment. The reason he gives in Daniel 10:11 is "for I have now been sent to you." That's plain and simple, and it's all about him being sent to Daniel.
Yes, friend. The verse says, "when he had said this to me, I stood up trembling" (Daniel 10:11). Shaky, but standing. That's me whenever somebody sneaks up behind me in the bakery.

Daniel does stand. Daniel 10:11 says, "when he had said this to me, I stood up trembling." Trembling, yes, but up on his feet. That's quite the comeback after being set on his hands and knees (Daniel 10:10).

Yes, friend. The one sent says, "your words were heard, and I have come in response to them" (Daniel 10:12). Daniel's words went somewhere, and they were heard. That's the opposite of talking into an empty bakery.

Daniel 10:12 says it right out: "your words were heard, and I have come in response to them." So the statement on the card holds. And it goes back to the first day Daniel purposed to understand and to humble himself before his God.

explanations.answer: The prince of the kingdom of Persia
explanations.explanation: That's the one, friend. Daniel 10:13 says, "the prince of the kingdom of Persia opposed me for twenty-one days." Daniel's words were heard from the first day (Daniel 10:12), and there was still opposition along the way. Then help arrived.

explanations.answer: The rulers of the land of Babylon
explanations.explanation: Babylon isn't in this verse at all. Daniel 10:13 says, "the prince of the kingdom of Persia opposed me for twenty-one days." That's the opposition named, friend. It lasted twenty-one days before Michael came to help.

explanations.answer: The armies of the king of Egypt
explanations.explanation: Egypt doesn't come up here, friend. Daniel 10:13 says, "the prince of the kingdom of Persia opposed me for twenty-one days." That's who stood in the way. Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help after that.
Michael, friend. Daniel 10:13 says, "Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me." That's after twenty-one days of opposition. Every crew needs one name it can count on.

Gabriel's a name you may know, but this verse doesn't use it. Daniel 10:13 says Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help. That's the name that fills the blank. He shows up after twenty-one days of opposition.

Elijah isn't in this scene, friend. Daniel 10:13 says Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help. That's who fills the blank. It happens after the prince of the kingdom of Persia opposes for twenty-one days.

explanations.answer: What will happen to Daniel's people in the latter days
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. He says he has come to explain "what will happen to your people in the latter days, for the vision concerns those days" (Daniel 10:14). Remember, Daniel 10:1 said the message concerned a great conflict. So there's a big picture coming.

explanations.answer: Why Daniel's men ran away and hid by the river
explanations.explanation: The men who hid don't come up in this verse, friend. Daniel 10:14 says he has come to explain "what will happen to your people in the latter days." That's what the vision is about. It concerns those days.

explanations.answer: How Daniel should bring his three weeks of mourning to an end
explanations.explanation: Nothing about ending the mourning in this verse. Daniel 10:14 says he has come to explain "what will happen to your people in the latter days." The vision concerns those days, friend. That's the focus.
That's it. Daniel says, "I set my face toward the ground and became speechless" (Daniel 10:15). Face down, no words. I think that's a very human response to everything he's just seen and heard.

explanations.answer: He gets up and walks away
explanations.explanation: Daniel doesn't go anywhere, friend. Daniel 10:15 says, "I set my face toward the ground and became speechless." He stays put, face down, with no words. Walking off isn't in the picture.

Daniel doesn't call anyone. Daniel 10:15 says, "I set my face toward the ground and became speechless." Calling out would take words, and he's got none right then. His men aren't mentioned in this verse at all.

Yes, friend. Daniel 10:16 says one with the likeness of a man touched his lips, and "I opened my mouth and said to the one standing before me…" Speechless in verse 15, talking in verse 16. Quite the turnaround.

Daniel does speak. Daniel 10:16 says one with the likeness of a man touched his lips, and "I opened my mouth and said to the one standing before me…" He's speechless in verse 15 and talking in verse 16. So the card's statement holds.

It's the other way around, friend. Daniel 10:18 says, "Again the one with the likeness of a man touched me and strengthened me." Daniel is not left to recover on his own. Help comes right back to him.

He doesn't leave. Daniel 10:18 says, "Again the one with the likeness of a man touched me and strengthened me." Daniel says he has no strength and no breath, and help is right there. That's a good friend move.

explanations.answer: Speak because you have strengthened me
explanations.explanation: That's what he says: "Speak, my lord, for you have strengthened me" (Daniel 10:19). Moments earlier he said no breath was left in him (Daniel 10:17). Now he's ready to listen. I wish my Monday mornings had that kind of turnaround.

explanations.answer: Give me time to catch my breath
explanations.explanation: Daniel doesn't ask for more time, friend. He says, "Speak, my lord, for you have strengthened me" (Daniel 10:19). He had said no breath was left in him (Daniel 10:17), but then he was strengthened. Now he's ready to hear.

explanations.answer: Let me rest until the morning
explanations.explanation: No rest request from Daniel. He says, "Speak, my lord, for you have strengthened me" (Daniel 10:19). The strengthening came first, friend. After that he's asking to be spoken to, not to sleep.

explanations.answer: To fight against the prince of Persia
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. He says, "I must return at once to fight against the prince of Persia" (Daniel 10:20). At once, no dawdling. Me, "at once" is what I say when I smell something in the oven.

explanations.answer: To bring back the men who hid
explanations.explanation: The men who hid aren't mentioned here, friend. In Daniel 10:20 he says, "I must return at once to fight against the prince of Persia." That's the reason he gives for going back. It's a fight, not a search party.

explanations.answer: To guard the bank of the Tigris
explanations.explanation: Nothing about guarding a riverbank in this verse. Daniel 10:20 says, "I must return at once to fight against the prince of Persia." That's what he's heading back for, friend. The Tigris doesn't come up.

explanations.answer: What is inscribed in the Book of Truth
explanations.explanation: That's it. He says, "But first I will tell you what is inscribed in the Book of Truth" (Daniel 10:21). The Book of Truth comes first, and the return to the fight comes after, friend.

explanations.answer: Where the men who hid have gone
explanations.explanation: Daniel 10:21 doesn't say a word about the men who hid. It says, "But first I will tell you what is inscribed in the Book of Truth." That's the thing he'll tell first, friend. The men don't come up.

explanations.answer: How long his mourning should last
explanations.explanation: Mourning time isn't the topic here. Daniel 10:21 says, "But first I will tell you what is inscribed in the Book of Truth." That's what comes first, friend. Nothing in the verse mentions how long Daniel should mourn.
